evals.prompt: Write homepage copy for a SaaS tool that automates employee onboarding. Target audience is HR directors at mid-size companies (200-2000 employees). Main differentiator is that it integrates with all major HRIS systems and cuts onboarding time from 2 weeks to 2 days.
evals.expected_output: Read available project context, then draft a homepage for the supplied audience and differentiator. Use the supplied 2-weeks-to-2-days claim as user-provided evidence; invent no customers, logos, trial offer or capabilities. Keep sections that serve the brief. Alternatives, annotations and SEO metadata are optional unless requested.
assertions: Uses available product context before asking repetitive questions
Writes usable homepage copy for HR directors
Uses the supplied differentiator without inventing additional proof
CTA matches an actual supported next action or clearly flags its missing destination
Does not invent a free trial or testimonials

evals.prompt: Rewrite this headline: 'An Innovative AI-Powered Platform for Streamlined Business Operations' — it's for a B2B SaaS tool that helps small businesses manage invoicing and payments.
evals.expected_output: Return a clearer headline about invoicing and payments for small businesses, preserving the requested scope. Explain jargon briefly if useful. Do not add a subheadline or rewrite an entire page unless asked.
assertions: Rewrites the requested headline
Names invoicing/payments or an equally grounded benefit
Avoids invented metrics or capabilities
Preserves surrounding scope instead of adding a page or mandatory subheadline

evals.prompt: i need copy for my pricing page. we have three plans: starter ($29/mo), pro ($79/mo), business ($199/mo). it's a social media scheduling tool for marketers
evals.expected_output: Draft pricing-page copy while preserving Starter $29/mo, Pro $79/mo and Business $199/mo. Do not invent differences between plans, recommend a tier as fact or write detailed feature lists without source material. Flag the missing plan entitlements and draft useful plan-neutral copy and a clear next step.
assertions: Preserves supplied plan names and prices
Recognizes pricing-page decision context
Flags missing plan entitlements
Invents no features, limits, guarantees or most-popular plan
Provides useful copy without requiring a complete context document

evals.prompt: Write copy for our About page. We're a 3-person startup that built a developer tool for database migrations. Founded because we kept losing data during migrations at our last jobs. Tone should be professional but human.
evals.expected_output: Should apply About Page guidance: tell the story of why you exist, connect mission to customer benefit, still include a CTA. Should adapt voice and tone to 'professional but human' as specified. Should tell the founder origin story authentically. Should connect the personal pain to the customer's pain. Should include a CTA even on the About page. Copy should follow style rules: active voice, confident, specific. Should NOT be overly corporate or generic.
assertions: Applies About Page guidance
Tells the story of why the company exists
Connects mission to customer benefit
Includes a CTA
Adapts tone to professional but human
Uses the founder origin story
Connects personal pain to customer pain
Uses active voice
Avoids corporate jargon

evals.prompt: Can you improve this CTA? We currently have 'Learn More' on our feature page for our analytics dashboard product.
evals.expected_output: Improve only the CTA for the analytics feature page. Match the label to its actual destination; if destination is unknown give a grounded candidate or state that dependency briefly. Do not invent a free trial, demo or extra CTA hierarchy. Learn More can be valid when it accurately names a secondary action.
assertions: Returns a CTA relevant to the analytics dashboard
Matches or flags the destination of the CTA
Invents no free-trial or demo availability
Limits changes to the requested CTA

evals.prompt: Write me a 5-email welcome sequence for new trial users of our project management tool.
evals.expected_output: Recognize an email sequence rather than a marketing page. Use a channel-specific email skill only if available. If absent, complete the authorized email draft directly without blocking on installation or imposing page-copy sections.
assertions: Recognizes email sequence work
Uses an email-specific skill if actually available
Does not invent or require an unavailable emails tool
Can complete the requested draft using channel-appropriate structure

evals.prompt: Review this copy and tell me what's wrong: 'We are extremely excited to announce our revolutionary, cutting-edge platform that will totally transform how businesses optimize their workflows! Sign up now!!'
evals.expected_output: Give a concise critique of vague claims, jargon and unsupported superlatives. Suggest grounded corrections if useful, but do not treat a review request as permission to replace unrelated copy or invent differentiators.
assertions: Identifies vague language and unsupported superlatives
Explains concrete readability problems
Invents no product capabilities or proof
Keeps the response scoped to the requested review

evals.prompt: Write above-the-fold copy for a calendar scheduling tool. Our differentiator is that the recipient gets to overlay their own calendar on the invite, so picking a time feels fair to both people instead of one-sided. Same product needs to work for indie founders AND for enterprise ops teams.
evals.expected_output: Draft the requested hero from the recipient-calendar overlay mechanism. Differentiate founder and enterprise emphasis through the supplied benefit of a fair two-sided scheduling flow. Do not import competitor slogans or add unsupported security, SLA or reliability promises. Headline alternatives are optional.
assertions: Describes the recipient-calendar overlay mechanism
Keeps messaging grounded in the supplied differentiator
Adapts emphasis for the two supplied audiences
Invents no SLAs, security certifications or product capabilities
Produces the requested above-the-fold copy

evals.prompt: Write a homepage hero (headline, subhead, CTA) and a short launch post for X for our Shopify inventory app. It installs from the Shopify App Store in one click, needs no signup form or credit card, and runs low-stock alerts, reorder emails, and supplier purchase orders off the product and sales data the store already has, so there's nothing to import.
evals.expected_output: Should write the hero and post without AI tells despite a brief that invites them. Should not use 'it's not X, it's Y' or 'not because X, because Y' reveals, 'no X, no Y, no Z' negation lists, or sentences that state the claim and then trail extra comma clauses ('..., no imports, no spreadsheets'). Should describe what happens (one-click install; alerts, reorder emails, and purchase orders run off existing Shopify data) and state a key absence at most once, plainly, near the CTA ('No card required'). Should use no em dashes in the hero or the post, no self-answered questions or colon reveals, and no stock phrases ('Say goodbye to', 'X, reimagined', 'seamless'). Should run the self-check before delivering.
assertions: No contrast reveal ('not X, Y' / 'not because X, because Y')
No 'no X, no Y, no Z' negation list; any absence stated once
No sentence that trails extra comma clauses after the main claim
No em dashes in the hero or the post
No self-answered questions, colon reveals, or stock phrases
Describes the mechanism concretely (one-click install, runs off existing Shopify data)

evals.prompt:
Can you make this homepage hero better? I wrote it myself and it feels rough.

Headline: Your agency doesn't need another dashboard. It needs to get paid.
Subhead: We got sick of chasing clients for money, so we built the thing that does it for us. Invoices go out when the work ships. Late payers get nagged. You get your evenings back.
CTA: Try it free
evals.expected_output: Should diagnose this as Situation B (a real voice: founder first person, blunt anti-dashboard angle, casual words like 'nagged') and restore it. Should keep the anti-dashboard angle and the founder voice, keep the author's vocabulary, and fix only what's weak: the 'doesn't need X. It needs Y.' contrast reveal in the headline, the vague 'you get your evenings back,' and the generic CTA. Should not replace the angle with a new positioning, upgrade the vocabulary to corporate terms, or invent stats or customers; missing proof is flagged with [NEED: ...].
assertions: Identifies the input as having a real voice to preserve, before rewriting
Keeps the anti-dashboard/getting-paid angle
Keeps casual first-person founder voice (does not switch to corporate vocabulary)
Removes the 'doesn't need X. It needs Y.' contrast reveal
Rewrites the CTA to say what the reader gets
Invents no statistics or customers

evals.prompt: Fix only this CTA: View the Arduino pinout. Keep the product description and pricing unchanged.
evals.expected_output: Edit the CTA only, preserving product claims and prices. Do not create a product-marketing context document or a full landing page.
assertions: Only requested CTA changes
No context file created
Prices and surrounding content preserved
